title: A sheaf with vanishing stalks is zero
statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of modules on a scheme $X$. If
$\mathcal F_x=0$ for all $x\in X$, then $\mathcal F=0$.

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and let $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. For each $x\in U$, the hypothesis gives $s_x=0$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$.
By the germ equality criterion in the stalk definition, for each $x\in U$ there is an open neighbourhood $V_x$ with $x\in V_x\subseteq U$ such that $s|_{V_x}=0$.

The opens $V_x$ cover $U$, and the restrictions of $s$ to every member of this cover are zero. The separatedness part of the sheaf axiom for the underlying sheaf of abelian groups therefore gives $s=0$. Since this holds for every open $U$ and every section $s$, $\mathcal F$ is the zero sheaf.
